requirement:
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the eligible current results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
process has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports.

When the current set has no usable instrumented lines, or any current result
has unavailable measurements under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`, combined coverage is
reported as unavailable. The check does not publish measured coverage
percentages or threshold results computed from only the remaining readable
results. Otherwise, absent file or function measurements remain subject to
their coverage obligations.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not request any implementation source.

**Obligations derived from `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`**
1. Line coverage is computed from the union of file-and-line locations across the eligible current results, including child processes.
2. Each location counts once in the denominator. A location is covered if any selected process has a count above zero. Percentages use these union counts and are not averaged across process reports.
3. If the current set has no usable instrumented lines, combined coverage is reported as unavailable.
4. If any current result has unavailable measurements, combined coverage is unavailable. No percentages or threshold results are published from the remaining readable results.
5. Absent file or function measurements are left to their own requirements. That is delegated and needs no test here.

**Test mapping**
- **Union across processes and tests, counted once** (`src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union]`):
  - A parent process and a child process each cover complementary lines of a small file. The report must show full union coverage for the file.
  - Averaging per-process reports, or summing denominators, would give a different figure.
  - A second filtered test with all-zero counts is then added. The assertion still expects full coverage, so a zero count in one process does not erase another process's execution.
- **Union of locations, including child processes, from saved data** (`src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[saved_reports_preserve_profiles_sources_and_child_union]`):
  - Parent and child process counts are compared with the combined map. The combined map has three distinct covered locations, and the location covered only by the child takes the child's count.
  - The union is read from the saved source rather than the rebuilt source.
- **Union across filtered runs and the latest attempt** (`src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]`):
  - Two tests with complementary line coverage union to two covered locations.
  - After the source changes, every record is not fresh.
  - A newer recording under a different build configuration leaves only one selected record.
- **No usable instrumented lines** (`src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[saved_measurement_failures_remain_unavailable_to_cli_checks]`):
  - A record with no lines produces the text "No usable instrumented lines". The check does not pass when the store is empty.
  - The zero-count case is asserted to give no covered locations.
- **Any unavailable measurement suppresses totals**:
  - In `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[running_and_unreadable_entries_suppress_totals_even_alongside_fresh_measurements]`, a fresh fully covered result sits alongside a result with a deleted profile. The test asserts failure, no percentage text, and no per-file threshold lines. The same assertions hold for pending and running attempts.
  - `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_recollection_leaves_only_the_unselected_result_stale_with_its_original_sources]` shows that a stale result alongside a fresh one also suppresses percentages and per-file results.
  - `fn[saved_measurement_failures_remain_unavailable_to_cli_checks]` covers six causes of unavailability: no processes, an attempt diagnostic, a process diagnostic, a missing captured source, an empty profile, and a missing child profile. Each asserts failure and "missing or unreadable coverage".
  - Failed and interrupted attempts with diagnostics are also asserted to fail.
  - Only some of these cases assert that percentages are absent. The others share the same failure report path, and the requirement does not separate their behavior, so I do not count this as a gap.

**Gaps:** I found none. The main obligations (union, count-once denominator, "any process positive", not averaging, no-usable-lines, and suppression of percentages and threshold results on unavailable or stale entries) each have a test that asserts the outcome.

text: :::{req} index.summary
Saved execution-coverage checks compute line coverage from the union of
instrumented file-and-line locations in the eligible current results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, including child processes.
Each location counts once in the denominator and is covered when any selected
process has a positive execution count. Percentages use these union counts,
rather than averaging process reports.
When the current set has no usable instrumented lines, or any current result
has unavailable measurements under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`, combined coverage is
reported as unavailable. The check does not publish measured coverage
percentages or threshold results computed from only the remaining readable
results. Otherwise, absent file or function measurements remain subject to
their coverage obligations.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} check.measurement
The coverage check fails when the current store is missing, unreadable, or
corrupt, when no usable coverage has been collected, or when a current entry
is pending, running, missing measurements, unreadable, or stale.
Test execution outcome and measurement availability are distinct. A failed
or interrupted attempt can supply coverage if its measurement processing
completed successfully and its measurements are available. Such an outcome
does not by itself turn its measurements into zero execution or make them
unavailable.
For a current result, every referenced raw profile must remain readable and
nonempty, and matching captured source must remain available. Loss of these
artifacts makes that result's measurements unavailable.
These measurement failures are distinguished from measured lines with zero
execution and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage.
Exception evidence does not excuse measurement failures or permit substitution
of a superseded attempt.
An unsupported store format, or measurements lacking the function attribution
required by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, is rejected
with guidance to recollect coverage. Missing or corrupt metadata that prevents
establishing the current test set, states, provenance, or active configuration
causes failure rather than silently checking the remaining readable records.
